identity.title: Monthly EHS Self-Check Form (blank internal template), Portland Facility

scan.summary: This is the company's own blank monthly checklist. It has eight lines covering the air permit, the scrubber and carbon-unit logs, forklift inspections, fire extinguishers, exits, eyewash stations and showers, and safety data sheets. It is a template, not a filled-in record, so it proves nothing yet. It becomes evidence only when someone completes it each month with Y/N, initials and a supervisor sign-off.
scan.freshness_note: The form has no date, revision number or month filled in. Because it is blank, how old it is doesn't matter much. What matters is whether completed copies exist for recent months, especially August and September 2026. Ask for those.

deadlines.title: Report any items marked N to the Plant Manager
deadlines.source_line: Items marked N are reported to the Plant Manager by the 5th of the following month.

facts.value: The form's acceptable range for scrubber pressure drop is 2.0 to 6.0. No units are given.
facts.affects: This is the internal range the scrubber log is checked against. It should match the range in the air permit (ACDP 26-2841-ST-01). I have not confirmed that it does.

facts.value: There is more than one eyewash station and safety shower at the site. The form does not say where they are.
facts.quote: Eyewash stations and safety showers flushed this week and logged
facts.affects: Confirms the site has emergency eyewash and shower equipment that needs weekly activation and a log.

expected_missing.title: Completed monthly self-checks for recent months
expected_missing.why: The blank form shows the process exists. Completed, signed copies are what show it was actually done.
expected_missing.basis: similar companies, not a checked requirement

expected_missing.title: Written Hazard Communication program, plus a chemical inventory / SDS binder index
expected_missing.why: Line 8 refers to an SDS binder index. No written HazCom program appears in what the company holds, and chemical makers and repackagers usually keep one.
expected_missing.basis: similar companies, not a checked requirement

expected_missing.title: Weekly eyewash and safety shower activation log
expected_missing.why: Line 7 refers to a log for eyewash and shower flushing, and it is not in what the company holds.
expected_missing.basis: similar companies, not a checked requirement

expected_missing.title: OSHA Form 300 Log and Form 301 incident reports for 2025
expected_missing.why: The company holds the 300A summary but not the log or incident reports behind it.
expected_missing.basis: similar companies, not a checked requirement

expected_missing.title: Exit route and exit sign inspection records
expected_missing.why: Line 6 checks exits and exit signs. Sites like this often keep a separate record of emergency lighting and exit sign tests.
expected_missing.basis: similar companies, not a checked requirement

expected_missing.title: Hazardous waste generator records and Oregon Community Right-to-Know / Tier II hazardous substance reporting
expected_missing.why: Chemical repackagers with bulk storage and tank farms usually hold these.
expected_missing.basis: similar companies, not a checked requirement

scan.confidence_notes: I'm sure this is a blank internal form. The month, the names, all eight Y/N and initials columns, and the supervisor sign-off are empty, so there is nothing to judge for completeness or recency. I did not check it against any rule, because no rule requires this exact form. Some things to review, not findings: (1) Line 2's range of 2.0 to 6.0 has no units and should be checked against the air permit's pressure-drop condition. (2) Line 5 matches the usual 12-month maintenance and monthly visual inspection for portable extinguishers under 29 CFR 1910.157(e), which Oregon OSHA adopts. I did not check whether Oregon's text differs. (3) Line 7 asks for weekly flushing, which matches the common ANSI Z358.1 practice. Neither the air permit posting nor the specific scrubber and C-1 conditions were checked against the permit text here.
